messages:
zoe: Quick sync — ran weight-only llm.int8 (bitsandbytes) on Orion-6.7B to exercise KV/prefix behavior and decode stability. Posting short summary and config we used.

maya: Nice, curious about perf / quality tradeoffs. what batch / kv settings?

zoe: Command: ```
python infra/quantize/run_quant.py \
  --model orion-6.7b \
  --method llm_int8 \
  --act-ordering perchannel \
  --blocksize 128 \
  --device a100:0 \
  --batch 8 \
  --stable-kv-cache True
```
Config notes: weight-only (no activation quant), per-channel scales, blocksize=128 to reduce bucketization artifacts. ran with prefix caching on and off.

ci-bot: benchmark finished — run_id=orion-int8-2029-09-09-01, artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-bench/orion/int8/run_1893456789 (metrics.json, samples.zip) :white_check_mark:

samir: numbers plz — latency / throughput / mem?

zoe: Short table (median of 5 runs):
- FP16 baseline: p99 latency=48ms token, median=31ms token, throughput=120 tok/s, mem=38GB
- INT8 weight-only: p99 latency=53ms token, median=28ms token, throughput=138 tok/s (+15%), mem=21GB (-45%)
Quality (GSM8K 4-shot subset): FP16 acc=72.6%, INT8 acc=71.4% (delta -1.2% absolute).

maya: Hmm p99 went up but median improved — makes sense if batching distributes differently. 1.2% on gsm8k is acceptable for many endpoints. Did you see any decode instability with cached prefixes?

zoe: Yes — felt a few deterministic mismatches when reusing long KV caches (>1024 tokens). Repro steps included sending same request in two ways: fresh context vs streamed prefix + new prompt. ~0.6% of samples had different final answers (not just whitespace). Logs show discrepant logits at early decode steps.

li: Curious — did you try toggling blocksize or quantization ordering? Might be rounding amplification across layers when cache is reused.

zoe: I re-ran with blocksize=64 and blocksize=256: blocksize=64 reduced mismatch rate to ~0.35% but slightly worse accuracy (-1.5%), blocksize=256 increased mismatch to ~0.9% but slightly better throughput. per-channel ordering seemed necessary; per-tensor made everything much worse.

rohit: For production, we should add a fallback policy for requests that are long-lived / use streaming prefix. Proposed policy: route low-latency short contexts to INT8, but for requests with prefix_length>512 or streaming=true, fallback to FP16. Thoughts?

maya: +1. Also we can provide a "stable_kv_cache" flag in the model profile that forces a slightly different quantization clip range to reduce divergence at the cost of ~2% memory.

zoe: example fallback snippet: ```json
{"routing": {"rules": [
  {"if": "prefix_length > 512 || streaming == true", "model": "orion-6.7b-fp16"},
  {"else": "orion-6.7b-int8"}
]}}
```
(we'll wire into Redwood routing layer)

samir: Any artifact on hallucinations or calibration drift? we should run some calibration evals (truthfulness/regression slices).

zoe: Quick check on truthfulness subset: FP16 truthfulness score=0.88, INT8=0.87. Most deltas are on numeric reasoning / multi-hop. Not catastrophic but measurable.

li: Action items: (1) run AWQ/GPTQ baseline on same model for a neutral comparison (2) run longer prefix stress test with streaming enabled and record mismatch traces (3) propose "stable_kv_cache" quant config that trades 3-5% mem for lower divergence.

rohit: I'll add a rollout plan: create a canary route for INT8 with the fallback rule and 10% traffic for internal services, monitor quality regressions on our eval hooks, auto-roll back if MMR (model metric regression) > 0.8%.

zoe: Sounds good. I'll kick off AWQ + GPTQ runs today and attach results here when done. For transparency, flagging that this INT8 weight-only profile is promising for throughput+cost but needs guardrails for streaming/long prefixes. :thinking_face:

ci-bot: scheduled job orion-awq-1893456789 queued (ETA ~3h)

maya: Thanks — if you can, include a small sample of discrepant decode traces (logits + tokens) so research can inspect where rounding diverges. even 10 examples will help.

zoe: Will do. Dropping 10 trace samples to the run artifacts later today.

samir: great thread. Can we also tag infra + runtime to check kernel selection behavior? there may be an edge with cached KV shapes changing kernel fast-paths.

zoe: tagging infra/runtime, cc @rohit for routing test.

li: I'll help design the "stable_kv_cache" config and do a quick simulation to estimate memory/latency impact.

rohit: plan posted to the rollout doc (internal) — linking once I add the rule. :shipit:

zoe: End of thread for now — will update when AWQ/GPTQ runs finish.
